rationale: EUDI PID Rulebook v1.6 s3.2 (SD-JWT VC encoding). The CLAIM names differ from the mdoc element names for the same attribute: birthdate (not birth_date), nationalities (not nationality), picture (not portrait). Claiming urn:eudi:pid:1 means meeting this list, not an arbitrary subset - a shorter list asserted a vct the credential did not satisfy (GAP-REGISTER G-19). place_of_birth is MANDATORY in the rulebook but omitted here: no evidence we hold carries a birth place, so it is omitted rather than invented (G-18).

claims.name: place_of_birth
claims.note: PID Rulebook §2 mandatory birth_place, §3.1.4/§4.1.1 place_of_birth: { ? country, ? region, ? locality }. Optional here - carried when the holder's passport or profile has it (captured at onboarding since 2026-09-30, G-18); David's call is that a PID needs no scanned document, so it is not refused without one.

claims.name: nationalities
claims.note: s3.1.3: [+ CountryCode], ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. A bare string would be a tstr, which is what the mDL wants and the PID does not.

claims.name: email
claims.note: Optional s3.2 claim, data identifier email_address.
